articles.descriptionJa: CJカーか、それともダリアン・メンサーか？ジョーダン・リードが、NFLドラフトのトップQB候補2人が激突する土曜日のマイアミ対ノートルダムの熱い対戦について考察する。
articles.body:
Week 10 of the 2026 college football season features some key quarterback matchups, none bigger than Miami's Darian Mensah facing Notre Dame's CJ Carr.

What does it mean for the 2027 NFL draft? Who has something to prove Saturday? Yes, the draft is still about six months away, but our analysts are always looking down the road, taking early notes on top players and starting to stack their rankings for an exciting class.

With that in mind, Mel Kiper Jr. and Jordan Reid will size up college football action through a draft-centric lens on Sundays all season long. They are answering lingering questions on the best 2027 prospects, sharing insights from scouts, picking out risers to watch and pulling back the curtain on their evaluation process. Here is what they saw and heard through Week 9 -- plus some lookahead intel on the Week 10 matchups.

Jump to:

Week 9 | Week 8 | Week 7 | Week 6

Week 5 | Week 4 | Week 3 | Week 2

Nov. 5

Who needs to have a big game more in their much anticipated head-to-head: Darian Mensah or CJ Carr?

Reid: Carr. I've seen both of these QBs up close on the scouting trail, and they have similar traits. Mensah and Carr are both extremely smart, accurate and always in command. Scouts I've spoken to over the past month have said they each have slightly above-average physical tools, and I have them as QB3 (Mensah) and QB4 (Carr) right now.

Over the past two games, though, Carr's ball placement has been a bit off. His worst performance of the season came against BYU in Week 8, when he completed 55.1% of his passes. Even though he bounced back and completed 65.5% of his throws against Navy, he was off-target quite a bit in that game, too. Miami's pass defense has been among the worst in the country, giving up 251.9 yards per game (122nd in FBS). Carr -- who plays like a more-mobile Kirk Cousins -- should be able to carve up that secondary.

Evaluators don't just need to see Carr win ... they want to see if he can be the reason the Fighting Irish win.

Which other QB are you most excited to see this weekend?

Reid: I have Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss vs. Georgia circled on the schedule. Chambliss has had plenty of success against the Bulldogs in previous matchups. In last season's College Football Playoff, Chambliss carved up the Georgia defense, finishing with 362 passing yards and two touchdown throws.

But the speed of the Georgia defense will challenge Chambliss and his ability to play within the pocket. When he reverts to ad-libbing outside of the structure of the offense, he could face many challenges. Chambliss will be one of the more polarizing prospects in this class because of his size (6-foot, 206 pounds) and age (turning 25 before next season). Sure, those are major talking points -- but it hasn't affected his game. He remains my QB2 behind Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker.

Nov. 1

True or false: Indiana receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh will both be top-20 picks.

Reid: True. Becker and Marsh are my WR2 and W

articles.descriptionJa: 今週の注目は何？マン・Uは巻き返しを狙い、コモの戦いぶりは魔法のように魅力的で、PSGは攻略すべき強敵、そして我々はジャンルイジ・ドンナルマのことが心配だ。
articles.body:
It's getting ridiculous in the best possible way. With each passing year, seemingly as teams realize that the extended Champions League league phase offers plenty of leeway if they lose a game or two, the guardrails slip a little bit more.

In 2024-25, teams averaged 1.63 goals per game in the league phase, a robust amount but not dramatically off of what we see in domestic leagues. In 2025-26, it was 1.69.

This year, through four matchdays, teams are averaging 2.02 goals per match and on Wednesday alone, six of nine matches saw at least five combined goals scored.

There were three 3-2 matches, including Fenerbahce's comeback win over Liverpool and lovely back-and-forth away wins for Manchester City (over RB Leipzig) and Real Madrid (over AEK Athens). And of course, there was Como's eye-popping 9-1 in over poor Lens; in their first Champions League campaign, the Italian side have scored 19 goals in their first four matches, winning three.

- UCL Talking Points: Are Como the real deal?

- Yamal makes more history for ruthless Barcelona

- Soccer's rich history of fan protests

The lack of consequence certainly has something to do with all this swashbuckling play, but maybe it's rubbed off on the rest of Europe? The season is still young, but scoring is up 7.8% in Ligue 1, 8.0% in the Bundesliga, 10.0% in LaLiga, and a whopping 20.1% in the Eredivisie and 23.9% in Serie A. Most of the increase has come from open-play, too -- it's not like teams are just earning a lot more penalties or something. (Meanwhile, Premier League scoring is actually down 2% so far this season. Fuddy duds.)

This is certainly a trend worth looking into, but for now I just want to say ... thank you. Goals are fun.

Let's once again look at five of soccer's main characters following another rousing Champions League matchday.

Main character No. 1: Manchester United's path forward

Ninety minutes is a long time. It's easy to forget that when you're an American fan accustomed to 3.5-hour American football games, but on Tuesday at Old Trafford, 90 minutes was long enough for Manchester United to play maybe their most listless 45 minutes of the 2020s (a high bar to clear), watch their fans rain tennis balls onto the pitch in protest of administrative incompetence and a nine-match winless streak, grab a lifeline in the form of a penalty, miss said penalty, take advantage of a second chance via VAR, spend a good 20 minutes blowing a number of great chances to tie, and still have enough time left to tie, take the lead and hold on for what might (or might not) be a season-saving and trajectory-defining win.

Roma's two early goals made United look completely hapless, and when United fell behind 2-0, it almost looked as if Bruno Fernandes started trying to pick a fight and land a red card so he wouldn't have to watch the rest of the match. It even took Fernandes a second penalty attempt to get the home team on the board.

articles.headlineJa: 2027年NFLドラフト・ビッグボード・ランキング：メル・キパーによるトップ25、ポジション別ベスト
articles.descriptionJa: トップ25にQBが7人も？今回のNFLドラフトは面白くなりそうだ。メル・キパー・ジュニアが11月初旬時点での最新ボードをまとめる。
articles.body:
I'm already getting excited for the 2027 NFL draft. This class could be really, really good. We have elite wide receivers, standout defenders and a bunch of excellent quarterback prospects. Roughly half the 2026 college football season is in the bank, and I'm updating my Big Board for 2027.

My normal disclaimer: This is not a mock draft. What follows isn't any form of prediction for when or where players will get picked once we hit Round 1 on April 29 in Washington D.C. Instead, this is simply my personal ranking of the best players in the class. The list below is based on my own evaluations from what I see on film and some conversations I've had around the NFL. And remember that a lot can change here. Players will rise and fall on the board, and some will even return to school for another year at the collegiate level before turning pro in the future.

Here is my current ranking of the top 25 prospects in the 2027 draft class, which includes a ton of QBs. And at the bottom, I've included the best players at each position. Check back regularly right through draft day -- I will keep this list updated as the class continues to take shape. But one spot that might not change at all is No. 1 ...

Jump to:

Positional rankings

1. Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

Height: 6-foot-4 | Weight: 222 pounds | Previous rank: 1

2026 stats over eight games: 62 catches, 1,067 receiving yards, 13 touchdown catches

Smith is very clearly the best player in this draft class. He's big, fast and physical, and he snatches the ball on the run cleanly. On 302 career targets, he has just six drops. And Smith has the body control to make tough catches. I love the way that he is always looking to improve, too. Smith worked on his after-the-catch skills heading into the 2026 season, and he has been able to make some things happen with the ball in his hands using his strength and speed.

Ohio State continues to feed him targets (north of 10 per game), and nobody can cover him. That was very apparent against Illinois in September, when he caught 12 balls for 217 yards and four touchdowns. In three seasons at Ohio State, he has 40 career touchdown catches, and he's averaging 16.1 yards per catch. Just an incredible football player.

2. Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State

Height: 6-3 | Weight: 215 | Previous rank: 2

2026 stats over eight games: 65.5% completion rate, 2,649 passing yards, 25 touchdown passes, seven interceptions; 227 rushing yards, two rushing touchdowns

Mestemaker didn't even start at quarterback for his high school team; he was the punter, played some safety and was the backup QB. Then he walked on at North Texas in 2024 as a QB before becoming the starter in 2025. After throwing for more than 4,000 yards, Mestemaker transferred with coach Eric Morris to Oklahoma State. It's an incredible story.

articles.descriptionJa: 木曜日のジャクソンビル・ジャグアーズ対ボルチモア・レイブンズ戦のベッティングに役立つオッズ、分析、予想。
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars rolled past the Indianapolis Colts last Sunday and are comfortably atop the AFC South. The Baltimore Ravens, on the other hand, have lost three straight and will start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano on Thursday with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both out. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and an interception in relief last week against the Buffalo Bills, and his first start comes on a short week against a Jaguars defense that allows 15.9 points per game (second fewest in the league) and generates pressure on 39% of dropbacks. It could be a long night for the Ravens if they fall behind.

Baltimore needs Derrick Henry to carry the offense. Jacksonville leads the league in run defense at 77.4 yards allowed per game but will be without DT DaVon Hamilton. On the offensive side for the Jaguars, running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. would have a larger role if Bhayshul Tuten is unable to go because of an ankle/foot injury. Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdown passes on only 14 attempts last week, and this is another game where he might not need to throw much.

Betting outlook

Jacksonville is favored by 10. Before Baltimore's quarterback injuries, the early market had the Ravens favored by three. That's a 13-point swing, and the over/under on the game total has dipped to 40.5. The market has already made a major adjustment, so I'm not rushing to lay double digits with the Jaguars on the road.

The Jaguars average only 59.1 plays per game (26th in the league) and run the ball on 48.3% of their snaps. That could help the Ravens stay within the number if Henry can keep the chains moving. The other possibility is Fagnano turns it over and gives Lawrence short fields. The Jaguars have scored 55 points off takeaways this season.

The player prop market may offer better value in this matchup. Lawrence averages a league-low 5.1 fourth-quarter dropbacks per game, and he could have another light workload if Jacksonville builds a lead. Henry has rushed for 58, 45 and 53 yards in his last three games, and the Jaguars have been stout against running backs.

Notable player props, bets

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Trevor Lawrence passing yards UNDER 235.5 (-112)

Moody: Lawrence is playing some of the best football of his career, but the Jaguars haven't needed him to throw often. He has gone under this line in four of seven games this season. If the Jaguars build an early lead against a Baltimore team starting an undrafted rookie quarterback, Lawrence may not have enough passing volume to clear this line. The biggest concern is Baltimore allowing a few explosive passing plays.

Trevor Lawrence rushing attempts OVER 3.5 (+101)

Matt Bowen: Lawrence has three rushing attempts in four straight games, but I think he will be forced to move outside of the pocket versus the Ravens defense on Thursday night. And let's remember that end-of-game kneel downs count here, too.

articles.headline: Portugal, Man United, Real Madrid: Cristiano Ronaldo's long history of rows with coaches
articles.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international soccer with Portugal after being benched by coach Jorge Jesus. It is far from the first high-profile row of his career.
articles.body:
Editor's note: This has been updated after Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international soccer on Nov. 5, 2026.

Was it always going to end like this? Cristiano Ronaldo -- Portugal's greatest-ever player, who led them to victory at the 2016 UEFA European Championship, and won the UEFA Champions League and the Ballon d'Or five times in a glittering club career -- has called time on his international career.

Ronaldo, 41, walked away from the national team's camp last month after a row with coach Jorge Jesus. The Portugal boss insisted there was "no issue," but admitted mistakes in his handling of Ronaldo's role in the 2-1 win over Norway in the UEFA Nations League on Sept. 27, when he was an unused substitute.

Despite it seeming as though the coach and his captain had patched things up, Ronaldo confirmed Thursday that he has played his last game for Portugal. However, an acrimonious end to his international career -- during which he has scored a men's record 146 goals -- could hardly be described as a shock.

- Ronaldo's incredible Portugal career: Best moments, key stats

- Siuuuu! The story of Ronaldo's career at Portugal, Man Utd, Real Madrid

- Ronaldo goal tracker: Every step on the road to 1,000 career goals

Managing the transition when an aging superstar's performance level drops is never easy, and Ronaldo's role and impact -- positive and negative -- with Portugal had been debated for three successive major tournaments: in 2022, 2024 and 2026.

Throughout his 25-year career, Ronaldo has been involved in a series of headline-grabbing disagreements with managers, teammates and executives. With his latest drama seemingly resolved, here are some of the most high-profile previous examples.

Unhappy Ronaldo backs Blatter's insensitive "slavery" comparison (July 10, 2008)

Ronaldo's bid to leave Manchester United for Real Madrid that summer reached a new, histrionic high -- or low -- when Ronaldo echoed comments from then-FIFA president Sepp Blatter that keeping a player at a club against their will was comparable to "modern slavery." Ronaldo told Portugal's TV1: "It's true. I agree with what the president of FIFA said. I know what I want and what I would like. We have to see what happens. I do not know where I will begin next season." After five successful years at Old Trafford, Ronaldo was ready to move on, but United stood firm and the forward had to wait another season before his desired move to the Bernabéu was finally fulfilled.

Ronaldo subs himself off mid-game at Old Trafford (Dec. 6, 2008)

Ronaldo abruptly walked off the pitch -- and headed straight down the tunnel -- midway through Manchester United's 1-0 win over Sunderland at Old Trafford. The team were left playing with 10 men, as United's coaching staff rushed to organise an unexpected substitution. ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Thursday

Klay Thompson makes his return to Golden State, where he won four championships. His Miami Heat are coming off an overtime win against the LA Clippers. In the only other game of the night, the Phoenix Suns will try to snap a four-game losing streak when they host the Orlando Magic. Both the Heat and Suns are playing on the second night of a back-to-back.

The Magic have lost two straight and remain without Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs. Franz Wagner has stepped up, averaging 20.3 PPG and 7.6 APG, and Anthony Black is off the injury report after missing Monday's game against the Washington Wizards. The Suns lost 132-119 to the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday despite 33 points from Devin Booker. Phoenix ranks last in defensive rating.

The Heat have won three of their last four games after starting the season 0-4. Thompson scored 30 points and made eight 3-pointers in Wednesday's win over the Clippers, including the game-winner in overtime. Bam Adebayo added 35 points and 10 rebounds, while Giannis Antetokounmpo finished with 27 points and 14 rebounds. Miami now faces a Golden State Warriors team that has won five straight. The short turnaround could be a challenge for Miami after Wednesday's overtime game.

Let's take a closer look at both matchups, along with some fantasy streamers and betting angles worth considering.

Fantasy stream team

Players available in at least 50% of leagues

 Anthony Black, PG/SG, Orlando Magic (rostered in 50.8% of ESPN leagues)

We're just over the roster threshold here. Black has taken on a larger with Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs sidelined. He has contributed as a scorer, playmaker and defender, finishing with at least 37 fantasy points in three of his last four games. Black sat out Monday's matchup against Washington, but he's off the injury report for Thursday's game against Phoenix.

Brooks has scored at least 29 fantasy points in three of his last four games and played 33 or more minutes in three of them. articles.headline: Mikel Arteta: Viktor Gyökeres 'really needed' a good Arsenal performance
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal forward Viktor Gyökeres "needed" a good performance after he starred in the 2-1 Champions League win at Slavia Prague.
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal forward Viktor Gyökeres "needed" a good performance after he starred in the 2-1 Champions League win at Slavia Prague.

Sweden striker Gyökeres made one goal and scored the other in one of his best displays since joining Arsenal in July 2025.

The 28-year-old has played second fiddle to Kai Havertz this season and had scored only one goal before Wednesday night, in the Carabao Cup penalty shoot-out defeat at Fleetwood last month.

But against Slavia, Gyökeres laid on the opener for Noni Madueke before scoring a stylish second on a hugely encouraging evening in the Czech capital.

"I thought he was really good," Arteta told reporters. "It was a game we believed would be really good for him, for the demands the opponent puts in and the spaces he could use.

"He's done it really well, not just for the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It's really great news for him, because he really needed that performance.

"He did that really well, understood really well when to appear, when to threaten, because they leave people, they follow man-to-man in the midfield and leave spaces there.

"So when I said he was really connected to the team, that was another example. I thought he had a great performance alongside the goal and assist.

"I'd imagine every player wants to play every game, and Viktor is no different. The players need to impact the game like he has done when they get the opportunity, to show the level they can produce. It's really positive for the team."

- Arteta: 'A lot to learn' from Arsenal's 'sloppy' win over Slavia Prague

- Kuyt hails 'another miracle in Istanbul' after Fenerbahce beat former club Liverpool

- Haaland tells Man City to 'step up' after netting winner in Leipzig

Despite his lack of minutes on the pitch, Gyökeres has now contributed to five goals in his last five matches.

"I feel very good," he told Arsenal's website. "Obviously, I'm happy with the win and to contribute to the two goals."

Premier League leaders Arsenal are up to third in the Champions League table despite a wobble in the second half, when Wiktor Nowak's 90th-minute goal left them clinging on throughout stoppage time.

"A good feeling in the first half -- and then obviously in the second half, with how that went, maybe the feeling isn't as good. But overall, if you look at the first half, it's a good feeling," added Gyökeres.

"It's my job as a striker and of course I want to contribute every game when I'm on the pitch and want to be involved as much as I can in attacks.

"So far we've had a good run in the Champions League and in the league as well.

"At the stage we're in right now, we're in a good spot, but I think we're all clear on what we can improve and what we need to do to take the next step."

articles.headline: Jack Grealish won't return for Everton this weekend - David Moyes
articles.description: Jack Grealish remains unavailable for Everton's Premier League clash with Coventry on Friday.
articles.body:
Jack Grealish remains unavailable for Everton's Premier League clash with Coventry on Friday.

The on-loan Manchester City midfielder has missed the Toffees' last two games -- both against Newcastle, in the Carabao Cup and the league -- following a breach of club discipline.

The club have given few details about the situation other than to say the 31-year-old was "not match-fit" prior to Monday's victory at St James' Park.

Manager David Moyes was again reluctant to discuss the matter at a press conference on Thursday but did confirm the England international would not feature against the Sky Blues at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Moyes said: "No, Jack is not available. I wouldn't give you the plan but we will be working with Jack again soon."

Asked if the upcoming international break could give Everton the opportunity to resolve the issue, Moyes added: "We just need to wait and see how things go."

- There is a way back for Jack Grealish after another Everton omission - David Moyes ESPN News Services

- Jack Grealish misses Everton-Newcastle due to 'breach of club discipline'

Moyes is hopeful defender Jarrad Branthwaite will be available after he was withdrawn with cramp in the latter stages on Monday.

He said: "We're just nursing him along a wee bit, just checking to see he's OK. We need to see how he is."

articles.headline: Harry Kane signs new Bayern Munich contract: 'I want to win many more titles'
articles.description: Harry Kane has signed a new contract to commit his future to Bayern Munich until 2029.
articles.body:
Harry Kane has signed a new contract to commit his future to Bayern Munich until 2029.

ESPN had previously reported that the Ballon d'Or winner, 33, was close to extending his stay with the German giants, after he entered the final season of the four-year deal he signed when joining Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023.

The England captain won football's top individual prize -- becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to do so -- after scoring 73 goals last season.

He ended his personal trophy drought by winning the Bundesliga in 2025 and 2026, and also won the German Cup last season. Kane scored 100 goals in Germany's top flight in the fewest games ever, managing the feat in just 98 appearances.

Kane also recently matched the record, held by Peter Shilton since 1990, for the most England caps after a 125th appearance against Czechia in the most recent international break. He was already his country's top goalscorer with a tally that stands at 91 goals.

Kane has scored 12 times for Bayern so far this season, giving him a tally of 156 goals in 161 appearances for the club.

"I feel right at home at FC Bayern," Kane said. "I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club."

Herbert Hainer, FC Bayern president, said: "What began as a major transfer has, over time, become a special chapter in FC Bayern's history. Harry Kane lives up to every promise football has to offer, and he has secured his place in the hearts of the fans as one of the greatest figures in the sport of our time. My compliments to Jan-Christian Dreesen and our sporting management team. This is a special moment for FC Bayern today."

Jan-Christian Dreesen, FC Bayern CEO, said: "We're delighted to have successfully extended Harry Kane's contract. This is fantastic news for us, for our fans and for the Bundesliga. The Ballon d'Or winner is staying at Bayern Munich! Since joining us in 2023, he has achieved extraordinary things with his goals, his influence on the game and as a role model both on and off the pitch. He has long since made FC Bayern his home, has continued to develop with us and crowned that development with the Ballon d'Or. His contract extension is a commitment to FC Bayern and to a story that is far from over."

Max Eberl, FC Bayern board member for sport, said: "This key contract extension gives us certainty in our planning. It sends a message that the biggest goals are within reach at FC Bayern. Players like Harry Kane offer a team unique opportunities. We're delighted that he will continue to be a key figure who helps shape the direction of the club, and with whom we can continue to build our squad for the future."

The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Nov. 5

Wemby makes MVP opening statement

Victor Wembanyama officially launched his 2027 NBA MVP campaign on Wednesday with a statistical performance not seen since Wilt Chamberlain.

The Spurs star posted 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks in a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks, becoming the first player to achieve a 52/24/8 line since blocks became an official statistic in 1973-74.

Chamberlain, the Hall of Fame center, is the only player in league history to match or exceed those numbers thanks to a 55-point, 29-rebound, 17-block performance for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks in 1961.

This was truly rare air: Wembanyama posted the NBA's first 52/24 line since Chamberlain in 1969 and the first 50-20 game since Luka Doncic in 2022.

"It should be more like this," Wembanyama promised. "More often."

With Doncic and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander emerging as early MVP favorites, Wembanyama threw his hat into the ring on a wild night that easily could have gotten even wilder. The 2023 No. 1 pick set a new career high for scoring by shooting 16-of-28 from the field and 19-of-23 from the free throw line against an overmatched Dallas front line, but he made only one of his eight 3-point attempts.

"I can still do more," Wembanyama said, noting that he's shooting a career-low 24 percent on 3-pointers this season. "My shots weren't falling tonight and that forces me into a style of play that is exhausting. I can do it. The proof is there."

After stumbling out of the gate with an 0-2 start, the Spurs have won six straight games and Wembanyama has started to find his scoring groove. The Thunder held the French center to 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting on opening night, but he has scored at least 36 points in three of his past four games and is on track to lead the NBA in blocks for the fourth straight season.

Go ahead and brace for more fireworks: Wembanyama and the Spurs are set to face the NBA's three worst defenses -- the Kings, Suns and Bulls -- over the next week.

Wembanyama, 22, finished third in MVP voting last season and is seeking to become the award's youngest winner since Derrick Rose in 2011.

Nov. 4

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Premier League clubs line up for Como defender
articles.description: Como center back Jacobo Ramón has caught the eye of Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal and Liverpool. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Como center back Jacobo Ramón has caught the eye of Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal and Liverpool, while Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri could join rivals United. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are one of several clubs keen on signing Como center back Jacobo Ramón, TEAMtalk reports. The 21-year-old, who transfer is valued at around €50 million, impressed the Red Devils during Como's 4-1 UEFA Champions League victory over them last month. Chelsea are also keen, while Arsenal, Liverpool and Fulham are monitoring his development in Italy. However, his former club Real Madrid are considering exercising their option to re-sign him next summer, potentially complicating any move from Premier League clubs.

- Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri could join rivals Manchester United, as he is seeking an exit in January, according to The Sun. Ait-Nouri, 25, has played only four times this season and has yet to appear in the Premier League. United are looking for a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw, and have been linked with Newcastle United's Lewis Hall, AFC Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, but could turn to the Algeria international.

- Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United have stepped up their scouting of Galatasaray attacking midfielder Alexsey Batrakov, according to TEAMtalk. All three clubs watched the 21-year-old score twice against Stuttgart on Tuesday evening in the UEFA Champions League. The Russia international is reported to have a release clause worth €60 million, although a January departure is considered unlikely as Gala are looking to open talks over an improved contract and could seek to remove the clause as part of any new agreement.

- Everton are interested in signing Palmeiras striker Vitor Roque in 2027, as per Diario Sport. The Brazilian club are unwilling to open negotiations at less than €50 million for the 21-year-old, whose contract runs until December 2029. A move could also provide a windfall for his former club Barcelona, who retained 20% of his economic rights after his move to Palmeiras last year and would receive €10 million from a transfer at that price. Roque has scored five goals in 19 league matches this season.

- Liverpool are in advanced talks with 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni over a contract extension, according to The Athletic. Discussions have been ongoing for several months, with all parties optimistic that an agreement will be reached, although nothing has been finalized. Nyoni has more than 3½ years remaining on his current deal, but Liverpool want to reward his progress under Andoni Iraola. The club rejected a £30 million offer from Nottingham Forest to sign him in the summer.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball rookie watch: Who's standing out and who's worth monitoring
articles.description: Eric Moody highlights which rookies are standing out in the early part of the NBA season, and which are worth rostering now or down the road.
articles.body:
The first two weeks of the season have already shown how differently these rookies are being used. Some have stepped into significant roles and are delivering for fantasy managers. Others are struggling with their shot or simply aren't getting enough minutes to make an impact.

Let's rank the top 15 rookies based primarily on their rest-of-season value in points leagues, with some consideration for category formats.

We'll also look at which players could become more fantasy relevant as the season progresses.

1. Caleb Wilson, SF, Chicago Bulls

Chicago hasn't wasted any time putting Wilson to work. The rookie has 19.5 PPG and 6.5 RPG in 34.1 MPG. He's also attempted 17.1 shots with a 26.3% usage rate. The shooting hasn't been particularly efficient, and averaging more than three combined steals and blocks will be difficult to sustain. Still, Wilson is getting plenty of opportunities on both ends of the floor. He's an automatic starter in fantasy lineups and has a chance to be especially valuable in category leagues.

2. Cameron Boozer, PF, Memphis Grizzlies

The shooting hasn't caught up with the rest of Boozer's game, but fantasy managers have a lot to like. He's averaged 16.5 PPG, 9.8 RPG and 5.4 assists while making 2.3 3-pointers per game. His 23.4% assist percentage shows how much Memphis relies on him as a passer. Boozer is also shooting 94.4% from the free throw line, which helps offset his field goal percentage below 40%. He's a strong hold in every format and someone I'd consider trading for if another manager is frustrated with his shooting.

3. Darius Acuff Jr., PG, Sacramento Kings

Sacramento has essentially given Acuff the keys to its offense. He's averaged 25.6 PPG, 7.0 APG and 3.0 3-pointers in 36.6 MPG, with a 32.3% usage rate. Acuff recently scored 38 points with nine 3-pointers against the Grizzlies. The downside is his efficiency. Acuff's shooting 37.7% from the field and committing 3.6 turnovers per game. That makes him more appealing in points leagues than category formats, but it's hard to argue with this kind of volume. Keep him in your starting lineup.

4. Yaxel Lendeborg, SF/PF, Golden State Warriors

Lendeborg has delivered in an expanded role for Golden State. He's averaged 21.5 PPG, 7.0 RPG, 3.9 APG and 2.5 3-pointers. Lendeborg's 63.8% true shooting percentage is impressive considering his offensive responsibilities. Jimmy Butler III's absence has helped create minutes and touches, and Lendeborg has played well. He's a must-start player, especially in category leagues. The one thing to watch is how much his role changes when Butler returns and Golden State's rotation gets healthier.

5. AJ Dybantsa, SF, Washington Wizards

Dybantsa missed the start of the season with an ankle injury, but the No. 1 overall pick has looked comfortable offensively through three games. He's averaged 16.5 PPG, 5.0 RPG and 1.0 SPG in 30.5 minutes per game. His limited assists and 3-point production make him somewhat dependent on scoring r
